incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for dedicated-pool eu-west-1-pool-7 — streaming stalls and queue depth rising > 1200. Auto-escalation triggered. Thread opened for triage.

Alice (oncall): ack. I’m on it. Paging eng-runtime and eng-sre.

Raj (eng-runtime): looking... I see sudden CPU/GPU allocation lag on pool-7, warmup tasks stuck in PENDING for ~45s. p95 ~800ms -> 2.6s, p99 trending 8-12s with streaming stalls.

Maya (eng-sre): confirming. autoscaler shows scale request at 1735554250 but pool handshake delayed; warmup heartbeat not received from new instances. queue_depth: 1287 -> 1432 in last 5m.

Alice (oncall): customer visible? Any 500s?

Leo (customer-success): a few customers flagged chats lagging; CS ticket #CS-1229 opened. Some customers reporting partial responses / truncated streams.

Raj (eng-runtime): root cause theory: dedicated autoscaler requested extra slots but the warmup handshake service (pool-init) hit a regression — NV driver init occasionally times out on that image variant. New instances stuck, not registering to router, so requests pile up.

Maya (eng-sre): reproduction logs: 
```
pool-init[pid=1224] WARN warmup: kv-cache restore timeout after 30s
kernel: NVRM: GPU init timeout
router: register failed: handshake deadline exceeded
```

Raj (eng-runtime): metrics snippet: 
- pool-7 active slots: 64/64
- pending_warmups: 12
- queue_depth: 1432
- p95: 2.6s p99: 11.3s
- streaming stalls: 1.9% -> 6.4%

Maya (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) divert non-critical traffic to fallback pool (eu-west-1-fallback) 2) manually scale another warm pool and warm a smaller instance with older image 3) enable degraded-mode streaming (reduce chunking) 4) notify customers and engage Dedicated ops.

Alice (oncall): do we have capacity in fallback?

Raj (eng-runtime): fallback has spare but lower throughput GPUs; it can handle reduced-CPU workloads. We should route lower-priority traffic and fall back to non-streaming responses for a subset.

Alice (oncall): OK do the traffic reroute. Raj, Maya, can you run manual scale and route rules? I’ll handle comms.

Maya (eng-sre): running commands now.
```
# manual scale warm node and kick warmup
redwoodctl pools scale --pool eu-west-1-pool-7 --delta 8 --reason "incident manual warmup"
redwoodctl warmup kick --pool eu-west-1-pool-7 --image-tag stable-2026-02-18
```

Maya (eng-sre): also applying route patch to spill traffic to fallback for customers in group low-priority: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --route default-chat --spillover eu-west-1-fallback --percent 30
```

Raj (eng-runtime): I’m temporarily disabling handshake strict-check to accept warm instances even if kv-cache restore not complete, so we register slots faster. Patch: 
```
# quick patch
edits in runtime config: handshake.strict_register=false
service restart runtime-router
```

Alice (oncall): heads-up: that relaxes correctness but prevents SLO collapse. Good for customer impact mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager: oncall engaged: Alice. Escalation level: SEV2. Notifying channel eng-runtime and eng-sre.

Maya (eng-sre): scaled +8 requested, 4 reached ready with older image; 4 still in warmup. queue_depth dropping to 980. p95 -> 1.4s p99 -> 4.2s. streaming stalls -> 3.1%.

Raj (eng-runtime): manually kicked warmup for the older image and registered nodes into router. Also toggled fallback variant for streaming -> chunked disabled for non-critical tenants. Running a probe to validate end-to-end.

Alice (oncall): update to customers: Leo, please send a short note to affected tenants: we’re seeing temporary latency due to capacity warmup, failing over some traffic to fallback pools, and expect progressive recovery in 10-20m.

Leo (customer-success): on it. Draft posted to CS channel and emailing top 5 tenants.

Maya (eng-sre): current numbers: queue_depth 420, p95 450ms, p99 1.2s, streaming stalls 0.9%. Manual mitigations holding.

Raj (eng-runtime): next steps: 1) roll back the image causing NV init flakiness (schedule a canary with the stable tag), 2) add a warmup retry and backoff in pool-init, 3) add a telemetry alert for warmup failure rate > 5% in 5m, 4) postmortem owner assigned.

Alice (oncall): assigning postmortem to Raj. Please include timeline, customer impact, and long-term fixes. Tag Maya for oncall runbook updates.

Raj (eng-runtime): noted. I’ll open PMR-487 (postmortem) and link this thread.

Maya (eng-sre): adding a short-term guardrail to autoscaler to not request > 6 nodes at once for that pool until we confirm image fix.

Alice (oncall): any residual customer errors?

Leo (customer-success): single ticket reopened but customers reporting improved experience. Will keep monitoring.

OpsRunbookBot: Runbook snippet matched: "Dedicated pool warmup failure". Suggested actions executed: scale, fallback, notify. Marking step 3 complete. Link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/warmup-failure

Alice (oncall): Great job everyone. I’ll hand off to next oncall in 20m with status summary. If anything degrades, re-open paging.

Raj (eng-runtime): logging action items in the incident doc now.

Maya (eng-sre): leaving a note in runbook to add image validation gate.

Alice (oncall): closing active mitigation — monitoring for 1h. Last numbers: queue_depth 120, p95 230ms, p99 580ms.

incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. SEV2 -> monitoring.

Alice (oncall): handing off to oncall-night (Tom) at 1735554700. See summary: warmup regression in pool-init caused autoscale delay, manual spillover and warm node scaling mitigated customer impact. Postmortem Raj/assigned.
